text: While your brain begins to starve for oxygen, an even more terrifying thermodynamic crisis immediately begins to unfold around you.
To understand why, ask yourself a simple question: what is heat?
In the realm of classical and statistical thermodynamics, temperature is not an independent physical substance.
Temperature is simply the kinetic velocity of jiggling atoms.
When a cup of water is boiling hot, its water molecules are violently thrashing and colliding with immense speed.
When water freezes into ice, those molecules slow down.
But if time is frozen, molecular motion drops to absolute zero.
The velocity of every particle outside your personal bubble becomes exactly zero meters per second.
By definition, the ambient temperature of the entire universe instantly plummets to absolute zero: minus two hundred and seventy-three point one five degrees Celsius.
Heat always seeks equilibrium, flowing aggressively from hot objects toward cold ones.
The frozen air resting against your skin instantly transforms into a catastrophic thermodynamic vacuum, voraciously draining the thermal energy directly out of your living cells.

Within just four seconds, the moisture on your lips, the tear film across your exposed corneas, and the capillaries inside your skin begin flash-freezing into rigid ice crystals, trapping you in agonizing cryogenic agony.
